NDT training in Detroit: how it works for Detroit employers and technicians

NDT training for Detroit and southeast Michigan employers and technicians is delivered by Atlantis NDT live online or onsite at your facility, under ASNT Level III oversight. Courses cover ASNT SNT-TC-1A Level I, II and III in UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET. Your employer issues certification under its written practice after documented classroom training, on-the-job experience, general, specific and practical exams and an annual vision test.

The overview above covers Detroit's automotive and defence base. This section goes deeper into the rest of the Detroit NDT economy, which is far broader than car plants: a refinery inside the city limits, a nuclear plant and major coal and gas plants downriver, integrated steel mills, international bridges, Great Lakes shipping and a vast supplier base making castings, forgings, welded assemblies and battery components. Each has its own methods, codes and certification expectations.

Atlantis does not operate a Detroit classroom. Theory is taught live online and practical training is delivered onsite at your plant or shop, which suits a region where suppliers are spread from Macomb County to Monroe and out to Livonia and Ann Arbor.

ASNT Level I, II and III courses available in Detroit

MethodLevelsWhat Detroit employers use it forPrerequisite
UT (Ultrasonic Testing)I, II, IIIResistance spot-weld evaluation on body structures, refinery corrosion monitoring, forging and plate inspection, structural weldsLevel I: none beyond the written practice. Level II: UT Level I plus experience
PAUT (Phased Array UT)II, IIISpot-weld and joining inspection with array probes, heavy weld inspection at power and steel plants, corrosion mappingNormally UT Level II
TOFD (Time of Flight Diffraction)II, IIICrack sizing on thick welds in power, refining and heavy equipmentNormally UT Level II
RT (Radiographic Testing)I, II, IIICasting porosity and shrinkage evaluation, pipe and vessel welds, digital radiography of componentsRadiation safety training plus NRC and Michigan requirements; RT Level I before Level II
MT (Magnetic Particle Testing)I, II, IIIForged crankshafts, gears and axles on wet bench units, steel mill equipment, structural weldsLevel I: none. Level II: MT Level I plus experience
PT (Liquid Penetrant Testing)I, II, IIIAluminium castings, non-ferrous parts, stainless welds, defence and aerospace supplier partsLevel I: none. Level II: PT Level I plus experience
VT (Visual Testing)I, II, IIIWeld workmanship, bridge and structural steel, plant equipment condition surveysLevel I: none; usually first
ET (Eddy Current Testing)I, II, IIIHigh-volume crack detection and material sorting on powertrain parts, heat exchanger and condenser tubingLevel I: none. Level II: ET Level I plus experience

Ultrasonic Testing. Detroit UT is unusually diverse. On one side sits resistance spot-weld inspection, where technicians evaluate nugget size and fusion in thin sheet using specialised probes and waveform interpretation; on the other, refinery and power-plant thickness surveys and angle-beam weld inspection to ASME. Our UT course covers the fundamentals common to both, then practical exercises weighted toward your application. Level II students learn to write techniques, evaluate indications and report to the governing specification.

Phased Array and TOFD. For UT Level II technicians. PAUT covers focal laws, sectorial and linear scans, encoding and scan plans, with examples ranging from joining inspection on vehicle structures to thick welds in heavy industry. TOFD covers diffraction sizing and its limits.

Radiographic Testing. Casting radiography is a Detroit speciality. The RT course covers exposure, geometry, image quality, film and digital radiography, and interpretation of porosity, shrinkage, inclusions and cracks in castings as well as welds. Computed tomography is introduced as context. Radiation licensing is covered in outline; it remains the employer's responsibility.

Magnetic Particle. Wet horizontal bench units testing forged and machined parts are a core Detroit application. The MT course covers head-shot and coil-shot technique, multidirectional magnetisation, field strength verification, fluorescent inspection, demagnetisation and the difference between relevant indications and non-relevant ones caused by geometry.

Liquid Penetrant. PT covers fluorescent and visible systems, sensitivity levels, removal methods, and process control checks such as system performance panels, which matter in production lines inspecting aluminium castings.

Visual Testing. VT covers direct and remote technique, weld and dimensional inspection, and documentation for structural and plant work.

Eddy Current Testing. ET is a production tool in the Detroit supply chain. The course covers impedance-plane analysis, frequency and probe selection, encircling and surface probes, and calibration standards, with applications in automated crack detection, heat-treat and material sorting, and exchanger tubing at power and process plants.

SNT-TC-1A certification path in Detroit, step by step

  1. Employer written practice, defining training, experience, exams, vision and recertification for each method and level.
  2. Classroom training completed to the written practice minimums. See our training requirements matrix for the figures by method and level.
  3. On-the-job experience, supervised and logged. Production-line technicians should log NDT time separately from other duties so it counts.
  4. General exam on principles.
  5. Specific exam on your employer's equipment, procedures and specifications, which in Detroit may be customer material specifications, ASME Section V, or AWS D1.1.
  6. Practical exam on flawed specimens, administered or overseen by the designated Level III.
  7. Vision test, near-vision and colour-contrast, annually.
  8. Employer certification, signed and filed.
  9. Recertification on the written practice interval.

Background on the framework is in our SNT-TC-1A guide.

Online, live-virtual or onsite NDT training for Detroit crews

  • Live online classroom, including sessions that fit second and third shifts. See online NDT training.
  • Onsite training at your plant, using your bench units, flaw detectors and part samples, so practical training reflects exactly what your inspectors see on the line.
  • Blended programmes with theory online and a compressed onsite practical and exam block.

Detroit scheduling follows model-year changeovers, plant shutdown weeks, and spring and autumn outages at refineries and power plants. Winter matters too: outdoor penetrant work on bridges and plant piping in cold weather requires procedures qualified for low temperatures. We schedule onsite blocks around your calendar and split groups so production continues. Send your headcount and window for a cohort or onsite quote within one business day. Ask about onsite training for your Detroit crew, or see our corporate NDT training programme.

Where NDT technicians work in Detroit

Automotive and mobility suppliers. Beyond the automakers, hundreds of Tier 1 and Tier 2 suppliers produce castings, forgings, stampings, welded assemblies and electrified powertrain components. Customer-specific requirements and quality frameworks such as IATF 16949 shape how NDT is controlled; SNT-TC-1A is widely used as the personnel qualification basis.

Refining. A Marathon Petroleum refinery operates in southwest Detroit and is a major source of turnaround and mechanical-integrity inspection work.

Power and nuclear. The Fermi 2 nuclear plant in Monroe County and large fossil generating stations downriver create outage work in UT, ET, VT and advanced UT. Nuclear owners apply ASME Section XI and their own programmes in addition to SNT-TC-1A.

Steel. Integrated steel operations in Dearborn and the downriver communities of River Rouge and Ecorse need inspection of cranes, rolls, structural steel and process equipment.

Bridges and border infrastructure. The Ambassador Bridge, the Gordie Howe International Bridge project and MDOT's bridge inventory all involve steel and weld inspection to AWS bridge requirements.

Defence and aerospace. Ground-vehicle defence programmes in Macomb County, Selfridge Air National Guard Base and aerospace suppliers in the region often qualify NDT personnel under NAS 410 or customer requirements. Atlantis does not offer NAS 410 certification.

Pipelines and utilities. Gas utilities and pipeline operators in southeast Michigan require weld inspection under API 1104 and PHMSA rules; the Michigan Public Service Commission oversees intrastate gas pipeline safety.

Industrial radiography in Michigan. Michigan is not an NRC Agreement State. The NRC, through its Region III office, licenses radioactive-material use in Michigan, including isotope radiography, and 10 CFR Part 34 requires radiographers to hold NRC-recognised radiographer certification. X-ray equipment is registered separately with the state Radiation Safety Section, now part of MIOSHA's Technical Services Division, which also reviews shielding plans for industrial X-ray installations. Your SNT-TC-1A RT certificate is separate from those requirements.

Across the river. Windsor, Ontario, is minutes away, and some Detroit companies work on both sides. In Canada, the national NDT certification scheme is CGSB under CAN/CGSB-48.9712 (ISO 9712). Atlantis training is SNT-TC-1A-based and suits employers working to US codes and for US customers; it does not provide CGSB certification. See our NDT salary guide for pay context on both sides of the border.

Level III services and written practices for Detroit NDT companies

Detroit suppliers often run NDT as part of a quality department rather than a standalone inspection company, and the written practice can drift out of date when a quality manager leaves or a new line adds ET or PAUT. Customer audits then find gaps. Atlantis provides:

  • Written practice development tailored to production NDT and plant inspection.
  • Outside Level III exam administration, specimen control and certification sign-off.
  • Record audits and recertification tracking across shifts.
  • ASNT Level III preparation for senior technicians and quality engineers.

Production NDT raises questions that field inspection companies rarely face. How do you certify an operator who runs one automated eddy current station and nothing else? Can a limited certification cover a single part family? How do you prove that the system performance panel on a penetrant line is checked every shift, and by whom? SNT-TC-1A allows an employer to define limited certifications and specific examinations in its written practice, but the document has to say so clearly, and the training and exams must match. We help Detroit suppliers write those provisions properly, so a customer auditor sees a controlled, defensible programme rather than a collection of informal sign-offs. For plants adding new processes, such as joining inspection on electrified-vehicle structures or battery enclosures, we review whether the existing written practice and procedures actually cover the new method and part, before the first production audit asks the same question.

Practise before the practical exam

Our Practical NDT 3D simulator lets trainees practise 12 methods across five environments: an NDT lab, a welding workshop, an aircraft hangar, an oil and gas site and a storage tank. Shift workers use it to rehearse technique between online sessions. It is practice only and does not replace hands-on training or the practical exam on real specimens.

Your instructor

Training is led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT, who oversees Atlantis course content, written practices and examinations.

Frequently asked questions about NDT training in Detroit

How do I get NDT certified in Detroit?

Work for an employer with an SNT-TC-1A written practice, complete classroom training and logged experience, pass general, specific and practical exams under a Level III, and pass a vision test. The employer certifies you.

Can I take NDT training online in Michigan?

Yes, for classroom hours your written practice accepts. Practical training and exams are hands-on and delivered onsite.

How long does UT Level 2 training take?

Classroom training takes weeks; the experience requirement takes months. See our training requirements matrix and your written practice.

Do I need a license for radiography in Michigan?

For isotope radiography the employer needs an NRC licence and radiographers need NRC-recognised radiographer certification. Industrial X-ray equipment must be registered with the state. Both are separate from SNT-TC-1A.

What does NDT training cost in Detroit?

It depends on method, level, group size and format. We do not publish prices; quotes come back within one business day. Request a Detroit training quote.

Is ASNT certification recognised by Detroit employers?

Yes. SNT-TC-1A is widely used across Detroit suppliers, refining, power and fabrication. Aerospace and some defence work uses NAS 410.

Do you have a training centre in Detroit?

No. Training is online and onsite at your facility.

Is spot-weld UT covered?

Our UT course covers the fundamentals and can include spot-weld practical work onsite using your equipment and parts.

Can a Detroit certification be used in Windsor?

Canadian employers usually require CGSB certification. SNT-TC-1A certification suits work to US codes and US customers.

Which method should I learn first?

In supplier plants, MT, PT or ET often come first; for plant and structural work, VT then UT.

Do you offer API or CWI training?

No. Atlantis trains to SNT-TC-1A only.

Can you train second- and third-shift inspectors?

Yes. Online sessions and onsite blocks can be scheduled around shifts.
